fieldValues.title: D2. Settle by principle: what we tried and where we went too far
fieldValues.thinking_reached: The ideal: a choice that a principle, charter cell, ADR or ruling already decides is settled where it arises, citing the rule, and never reaches the owner. What happened: of 24 needs-input questions on 2026-10-27, 15 were answerable from the charter, ADRs and rulings and 3 were real (finding e832c6f4). The owner reports that many decisions vanished once a review of principles was prompted (vignette 3e076051). Remedy e120cf12 (apply the charter before escalating) is suggested. What works: srs and srs-rust have a long history of deciding by compass and principles (owner, vignette, 2026-10-28). The decision compass (srs/docs/charter/decision-compass.md, since 2026-08-23) with its Charter Check, and srs-rust ADR-048, settle most choices where they arise: 41 of 54 srs rfc-decision records cite the compass, a cell or an axis. The programme layer has no equivalent in use (SP-72: a group has no affirmed compass of its own), so its choices escalate instead.
fieldValues.tensions: Escalate to be safe, and decide by the rule already set. Too far toward escalating: the owner receives what principles settle (SP-63, SP-99).
fieldValues.unresolved_questions: Which principles settle most, and which choices recur because no principle covers them?
fieldValues.next_action: Each escalation that a principle settles is a decision-stop finding here, naming the principle.
